rows.figure: 1:15 fatal to nonfatal ambulance-attended drowning incidents (Table 1: 1:15.35; 243 fatal, 3,730 nonfatal, 3,973 total)
rows.scope: New South Wales, 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2021, all ages. Cohort is every person attended by a NSW ambulance for drowning (3,973), linked to emergency-department and death-registry records; fatal means a death date within 30 days of the ambulance attendance (243), nonfatal is the rest (3,730). Leaves out people who reached hospital without an ambulance, people who never sought care, and drowning deaths with no ambulance attendance, so the fatal count is not the state's drowning-death total.
rows.source: Journal of Safety Research 2024;91:373–380, 'Rates and ratios of fatal and nonfatal drowning attended by ambulance in New South Wales, Australia between 2010 and 2021', DOI 10.1016/j.jsr.2024.09.019 (published version, CC BY 4.0, in the authors' university repository ResearchOnline@JCU)
rows.do_not_add_to: An ambulance-attendance ratio for one Australian state; not an emergency-department, hospitalisation or claims ratio, not national or global, and never averaged with ratios that use a different denominator or place.
rows.note: Printed as 1:15 in the Abstract (p. 373) and as '15 nonfatal drownings for every fatality' in the Discussion (p. 375); as 1:15.35 in Table 1 and the Results (p. 374). Sub-group ratios in the same paper: 10–19 year-olds 1:77, females 1:22, metropolitan 1:20, residential 1:23. The publisher's ScienceDirect page is closed to this agent (robots), so the paper was read from the repository copy; the abstract's page number is inferred from the article's page range.

rows.figure: 6.9 drowning-related hospitalisations for every one fatal drowning, children under five (Table 2: 27 fatal, 185 hospitalisations)
rows.scope: Aotearoa New Zealand, children aged 0–4, 2012–2017, the years for which ACC data were available (the paper's fatal and hospitalisation series otherwise run 2005–2019). Fatal unintentional drownings and drowning-related hospitalisations from Water Safety New Zealand's DrownBase; Table 2 gives 27 fatal and 185 hospitalisations. Leaves out children treated only in an emergency department or in primary care and any child not admitted to hospital.
rows.source: Australian and New Zealand Journal of Public Health 2022;46(1):46–51, 'Quantifying fatal and non-fatal drowning in children under five in Aotearoa, New Zealand', DOI 10.1111/1753-6405.13157, PMID 34529307 (published version, CC BY-NC-ND, read from a university repository copy)
rows.do_not_add_to: A hospitalisation ratio for one age group (0–4) in one country over 2012–2017; not all ages, not an emergency-department, ambulance or claims ratio, and never averaged with the 74.7 ACC-claims ratio from the same paper or with other places.
rows.note: The Abstract (p. 46) states the ratio without years; the Results sentence (p. 49) and Table 2 tie it to 2012–2017. The Discussion (p. 49) rounds it to 'seven'. Table 2 sub-groups range from 3.4 (age 1) to 15.0 (0–11 months). The publisher's page (the DOI now resolves to Elsevier) is closed to this agent; the Europe PMC record confirms the citation and abstract.

rows.figure: 74.7 ACC drowning-related claims for every one fatal drowning, children under five (Table 2: 27 fatal, 2,016 claims)
rows.scope: Aotearoa New Zealand, children aged 0–4, 2012–2017. Numerator is claims to ACC (the crown entity that administers the no-fault accident injury compensation scheme) identified as drowning-related by the word DROWN in free text, a drowning contact code or a read code of Drown or Submersion (2,016 claims); denominator is fatal unintentional drownings from DrownBase (27). Claims cast a far wider net than hospital admissions (2,016 claims against 185 hospitalisations in the same years).
rows.source: Australian and New Zealand Journal of Public Health 2022;46(1):46–51, 'Quantifying fatal and non-fatal drowning in children under five in Aotearoa, New Zealand', DOI 10.1111/1753-6405.13157, PMID 34529307 (published version, CC BY-NC-ND, read from a university repository copy)
rows.do_not_add_to: An insurance-claims ratio for children 0–4 in one country, 2012–2017; not comparable with hospitalisation, emergency-department or ambulance ratios, and never averaged with them or with the 6.9 hospitalisation ratio from the same paper.
rows.note: The Discussion (p. 49) rounds it to '75 ACC claims'. Table 2 sub-groups range from 18.0 (age 1) to 326.5 (age 4). The Abstract states the ratio without years; the Results sentence (p. 49) and Table 2 give 2012–2017, the only years ACC data were available (Methods, p. 47).

rows.figure: for every 1 fatal drownings there are 6 non-fatal drownings
rows.scope: Alberta, 1999–2019, all ages, from the Lifesaving Society Alberta and Northwest Territories and Injury Prevention Centre 20-year analysis of Alberta Health Line by Line Database. The post does not say what counts as a non-fatal drowning in the ratio; the companion infographic (July 2021) words it as non-fatal drownings 'that resulted in an emergency department visit or hospitalization', with the number in a graphic that could not be read. The post also prints '30 fatal drownings, and 24 non-fatal drowning hospital admissions from 1999-2019' without saying whether these are annual averages.
rows.source: Lifesaving Society Alberta and Northwest Territories, news post '20 Year Analysis on Drowning', 28 July 2021, announcing the 20-year Alberta drowning analysis done with the Injury Prevention Centre
rows.do_not_add_to: An organisation's rounded statement for one province with the denominator not stated on the page; not comparable with ambulance, hospitalisation-only or claims ratios, never averaged with the 'about five' in the 2022 Alberta Non-fatal Drownings report, and not global.
rows.note: The society's site also carries the Alberta Non-fatal Drownings: 2022 Report, which says 'about five' per fatal drowning counting emergency-department visits only (row alberta-nonfatal-ed-ratio-2022-report); the two are recorded separately, not reconciled. The post's '30 fatal drownings' and '24 non-fatal drowning hospital admissions' match the 2022 report's p. 1 callouts '30 Deaths (2000 - 2019)' and '24 Hospital Admissions (2001 - 2020)', which that report presents beside per-year averages, but the post itself never says 'per year'.

rows.figure: about five non-fatal drownings serious enough to require an emergency department visit for every fatal drowning
rows.scope: Alberta, all ages. The ratio sentence on p. 1 of the Alberta Non-fatal Drownings: 2022 Report gives no years and names no data source; the report's annual charts cover 2011–2020 and its p. 1 callouts read '30 Deaths (2000 - 2019)', '24 Hospital Admissions (2001 - 2020)' and '160 Emergency Dept. Visits (2001 - 2020)', with the text calling 160 'an average ... per year'. Counts emergency-department visits only; hospital admissions are reported separately (p. 2: 'average of 40 hospital admissions ... per year', 2011–2020).
rows.source: Injury Prevention Centre (University of Alberta) with the Lifesaving Society Alberta and Northwest Territories, 'Alberta Non-fatal Drownings: 2022 Report', September 2022, p. 1, hosted on the society's Drowning Reports page
rows.do_not_add_to: An emergency-department ratio for one province, printed as 'about five' with no years; not comparable with the society's 2021 '6' (a different document and, per its infographic, emergency-department plus hospital cases), nor with ambulance, hospitalisation-only or claims ratios; never averaged.
rows.note: Added because the lab records both figures when an organisation's own documents disagree; drop if out of scope. Text extraction dropped the 'fi' ligature so the sentence reads 'about ve'; a person should confirm 'five' in the PDF. The report's hospital-admission figures disagree internally (callout '24 Hospital Admissions (2001 - 2020)' on p. 1 against 'average of 40 ... per year' for 2011–2020 on p. 2).
